questions.stem: A length is measured as 4.5 cm, correct to 1 decimal place. What are the upper and lower bounds?
questions.explanation: Correct to 1 d.p., the error interval is +/- 0.05. Lower bound = 4.5 - 0.05 = 4.45 cm. Upper bound = 4.5 + 0.05 = 4.55 cm.

questions.stem: A rectangle has length 12 cm and width 5 cm, both measured to the nearest cm. What is the upper bound of the area?
questions.explanation: Upper bound of length = 12.5 cm, upper bound of width = 5.5 cm. Upper bound of area = 12.5 x 5.5 = 68.75 cm^2.

questions.stem: A distance is 240 km to the nearest 10 km and the time is 3 hours to the nearest hour. What is the lower bound of the speed?
questions.explanation: For the lower bound of speed = distance/time, use the lower bound of distance and the upper bound of time. Lower bound distance = 235 km, upper bound time = 3.5 hours. Lower bound speed = 235 / 3.5 = 67.1 km/h (to 1 d.p.).

questions.stem: x = 6.4 correct to 1 decimal place. What is the error interval for x?
questions.explanation: When a value is rounded, the lower bound is included (<=) but the upper bound is excluded (<), since a value of exactly 6.45 would round up to 6.5. So 6.35 <= x < 6.45.

questions.stem: p = 8.2 and q = 3.6, both correct to 1 decimal place. Calculate the upper bound of p - q.
questions.explanation: For the upper bound of a subtraction, use the upper bound of the first value and the lower bound of the second. Upper bound of p = 8.25, lower bound of q = 3.55. Upper bound of p - q = 8.25 - 3.55 = 4.70.
